name: copilotkit
summary: I successfully scaffolded the Next.js app, installed all CopilotKit packages, and configured the API route, layout provider, and sidebar component exactly per the quickstart. The dev server starts and serves on port 3000, and the `/api/copilotkit` endpoint demonstrably responds to POST requests—returning `{"error":"invalid_request","message":"Missing method field"}` when called without a proper body, which proves the CopilotRuntime handler is active. TypeScript compilation also passes cleanly. However, the production build (`next build`) repeatedly gets killed, likely due to sandbox resource limits when bundling the heavy CopilotKit dependencies, and no real OpenAI API key was present in the environment, so I could not verify an actual LLM chat response.

installed.evidence: added 856 packages, and audited 1222 packages in 1m

friction.detail: next build repeatedly OOMs/gets killed even with 8GB Node heap, suggesting CopilotKit dependencies are too heavy for standard sandbox limits. Quote: "Killed"
Setting turbopack: false in next.config.ts triggers a validation warning in Next.js 16.3.0 and does not disable it. Quote: "Expected object, received boolean at \"turbopack\""
No real OpenAI key was available in the sandbox, forcing a dummy key that prevents actual LLM verification. Quote: "No OPENAI_API_KEY found in env"

The exact Next.js app-router export name had to be grepped from inside node_modules, indicating the docs may not spell out the import clearly. Quote: "grep -r \"copilotRuntimeNextJSAppRouterEndpoint\" /home/daytona/my-copilot-app/node_modules/@copilotkit/runtime/dist/ --include=\"*.d.mts\" | head -5"
npm install emits multiple deprecation warnings and 13 audit vulnerabilities, which can distract first-time developers. Quote: "13 vulnerabilities (2 low, 10 moderate, 1 high)"
